title: kate-core: a changed file after delete is modified
summary: note_disk marks Created only when a deleted path returns with the same digest. A different digest is Modified. The test goes in the existing document tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

definitions.definition: pub fn note_disk(&mut self, exists: bool, digest: [u8; 32])

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: document.rs has one test module named tests.  Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Do not add a second module with the same name. Edit only the match inside note_disk. Paste this exact match. false returns Some(DiskChange::Deleted). true, when disk_change is Deleted and digest equals digest_on_disk, returns Some(DiskChange::Created). true, when digest differs from digest_on_disk, returns Some(DiskChange::Modified). true in every other case returns None. Do not assign digest_on_disk. Do not touch reload_choice, sentence, reload_prompt_line, from_loaded, or FileState fields. The existing test note_disk_names_modified_deleted_and_created stays green. Add a_changed_file_after_delete_is_modified in that same module. Start from file_state. Call note_disk(false, stored). Build other by adding 1 to stored[0] with wrapping_add. note_disk(true, other) leaves disk_change equal to Some(DiskChange::Modified). digest_on_disk stays equal to stored. note_disk(false, other) then note_disk(true, stored) leaves disk_change equal to Some(DiskChange::Created). Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines.

regression_tests.name: document::tests::a_changed_file_after_delete_is_modified
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main. A deleted file that returns with a different digest is Created. After the change it is Modified and digest_on_disk stays the stored digest. The same digest after a delete is still Created.
